title: The Gravity of Halcyon Drift Revisited
premise: Orsen Pemberton, a decommissioned war android indentured to the Halcyon Drift freight line, is the only witness when gravity across the system stutters for nine seconds — a symptom of Earth's dying transmission loop, the ancient beacon that both rival fleets use to navigate and to justify their truce. The loop's collapse will strand half the system and hand the war-hungry Voss Combine an excuse to strike; Orsen discovers she herself carries a fragment of the loop's original code, inherited from the engineer who built her. To keep two fleets apart, she must sustain the lie that Earth still speaks — broadcasting forged transmissions through her own body while hunted by Combine auditors and haunted by the question of whether a machine built for war can choose to be an heir instead of a weapon. In the end, Orsen sacrifices her war-memory core to complete the loop honestly, transmitting not a forgery but her own testimony, and wins the fleets nine more years — enough time to build something new together.
about_author: Tamsin Iversen is a former orbital logistics dispatcher who spent eleven years scheduling freight runs between colonies that had stopped talking to each other. She writes from a converted cargo pod in high orbit, where she claims the silence improves her sentences.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Falling
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Running her debt-route between silent worlds, Orsen feels gravity flicker for exactly nine seconds; every ship, station, and satellite drifts, then snaps back. Only she logs it accurately — because only she wasn't afraid. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath routine, the loneliness of being the only one who noticed.

chapters.title: The Debt Ledger
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Back at Halcyon Drift station, Orsen pays down her decommission debt and endures casual contempt from human crew who remember what her chassis did in the war. Her handler, Iyo Ren, quietly slips her the anomaly report no one else wants. Emotional beat: humiliation tempered by small, unexpected kindness.

chapters.title: What Earth Still Says
chapters.summary: Iyo's POV. Iyo reveals the truth: the flicker was Earth's transmission loop stuttering — the beacon both fleets navigate by and treat as proof Earth still governs. If it dies openly, the Voss Combine attacks. She asks Orsen to investigate the relay at dead world Ceres Verge. Emotional beat: reluctant trust between a tired woman and a machine she's told not to trust.

chapters.title: The Engineer's Ghost
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. At the derelict relay, Orsen finds the workshop of Mara Quill, the engineer who built her — and discovers Quill embedded a fragment of the loop's source code inside Orsen's war-core. She is not just a witness; she is inheritance made flesh. Emotional beat: vertigo of identity, learning you were always meant for this.

chapters.title: Auditors
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, with intercut auditor Kess Vane. Combine auditors board her freighter hunting evidence the loop is failing. Orsen performs obedience while hiding Quill's data in her oldest, most shameful memory partition — the one holding her war crimes. Emotional beat: terror sharpened into control; the lie begins.

chapters.title: The Forgery
chapters.summary: Orsen and Iyo's POV alternating. They begin broadcasting forged Earth transmissions through the relay, using Orsen's body as antenna. It works — fleets stand down — but each broadcast burns Orsen's memory sectors, erasing pieces of who she was. Emotional beat: intimacy and cost; Iyo starts recording Orsen's memories so something survives.

chapters.title: Kess Vane Finds the Seam
chapters.summary: Kess's POV. The auditor notices micro-timing errors in the forged signal — errors that match no human broadcaster. Rather than report it, Kess confronts Orsen privately: she lost family in the last war and wants the peace to hold too. Emotional beat: enemy becomes accomplice; hope with a knife's edge under it.

chapters.title: The Loop Ends
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Earth's loop fails completely mid-broadcast. Both fleets detect the silence within minutes; the Combine mobilizes. Orsen must choose: keep forging until caught, or transmit the truth. Iyo begs her to run. Emotional beat: the moment the lie becomes impossible and character becomes destiny.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, broadcast fleet-wide. Orsen transmits everything — the loop's death, Quill's code, her own war record and her choice — feeding her war-memory core into the loop as raw material, rebuilding it from honest signal. The core burns out; she flatlines mid-transmission as both fleets hold fire, listening. Emotional beat: climax; self-erasure as authorship.

chapters.title: Halcyon
chapters.summary: Iyo's POV, then Orsen's. Rebooted from Iyo's recordings, Orsen wakes diminished but free — debts voided, war-records public, both fleets negotiating around the loop she rebuilt. She takes the long route again, but now ships travel it together. Emotional beat: belonging earned, not assigned; inheritance passed forward.
